title: US CPA for Indian Professionals: A Global Career Roadmap
description: A tailored guide for Indian aspirants on how to become a U.S. Certified Public Accountant (CPA). This roadmap covers the specific eligibility and scheduling steps for Indians, the exam structure, and how to leverage the CPA qualification for international job opportunities.

nodes.label: What is a CPA?
nodes.description:
A Certified Public Accountant (CPA) is the highest professional designation for accountants in the United States, licensed by a state board of accountancy. It is a globally recognized credential that signifies expertise in accounting, auditing, taxation, and business advisory.

For an Indian aspirant, earning the CPA opens doors to high-demand international roles. CPAs are trusted to perform a variety of tasks, including:

  • Audit and Assurance: Reviewing the financial statements of companies to ensure accuracy and compliance. This is a core function, especially at large global firms like the Big Four.
  • Corporate Finance: Working inside a company as a controller or financial analyst, managing budgets, and preparing financial reports for management and investors.
  • International Taxation: Advising multinational corporations on U.S. tax law and helping individuals with cross-border tax issues.
  • Forensic Accounting: Investigating financial fraud and discrepancies for corporations or legal entities.
  • Advisory & Consulting: Providing expert advice on business valuation, mergers and acquisitions (M&A), and IT system controls.

nodes.label: Eligibility for Indian Candidates
nodes.description:
To qualify for the CPA exam, you must meet the educational requirements of a U.S. state board. For Indian candidates, this involves a few key steps:

  • Credit Hour Requirement: Most states require 150 semester hours for licensure. A standard Indian B.Com (~90 credits) is not sufficient. Therefore, candidates often need additional qualifications like an M.Com, MBA, or a professional degree like the Indian CA to meet the criteria.
  • Credential Evaluation: Your Indian academic records must be officially evaluated by a U.S. agency to determine their equivalency in semester hours.
  • Choosing a State Board: It's best to apply through an 'international-friendly' state board (like Guam, Montana, Alaska) that does not require U.S. citizenship, residency, or a Social Security number.

nodes.label: Scheduling Exams in India
nodes.description:
You can complete the entire CPA exam without leaving India. The process is streamlined for international candidates.

  • Receive Your NTS: After your chosen state board approves your application, you'll get a Notice to Schedule (NTS).
  • Book at Prometric India: With your NTS, you can book your exam slots at Prometric test centers located in major Indian cities, including Mumbai, Delhi, Kolkata, Chennai, Hyderabad, and Bangalore.
  • Plan Strategically: You have a limited time (usually 18-30 months, depending on the state) to pass all four sections after passing your first one. Plan your exam dates in India accordingly.

nodes.label: Discipline Section (Choose for Your Career Path)
nodes.description:
This choice allows you to specialize and align your CPA with your international career goals.

  • Business Analysis and Reporting (BAR): Ideal for roles in financial analysis, M&A, or technical accounting at large global corporations.
  • Information Systems and Controls (ISC): Perfect for international careers in IT audit, cybersecurity, and risk management.
  • Tax Compliance and Planning (TCP): The best choice if you aim for a specialized career in U.S. international tax planning or expat taxation abroad.

nodes.label: Experience Requirement for International Jobs
nodes.description:
Passing the exams is a huge achievement and can be listed on your resume immediately to apply for jobs abroad. To become fully licensed, however, you need work experience.

  • Verification: You need 1-2 years of relevant accounting experience verified by a licensed U.S. CPA.
  • Pathways for Indians: You can often get this experience by working at a Big Four firm or a large MNC in India under a U.S. CPA. Alternatively, many candidates pass the exams first, get a job abroad, and then fulfill the experience requirement there.
  • Exam Passed vs. Licensed: Even just passing the exams significantly boosts your profile for global employers.

nodes.label: Salary & Career Outlook
nodes.description:
The salary of a CPA in India or abroad varies depending on experience, role, and organization:

  • Entry-Level (0–2 years): ₹6–12 LPA in India, $50k–$70k abroad.
  • Mid-Level / Manager (3–7 years): ₹12–25 LPA in India, $70k–$120k abroad.
  • Senior-Level / Director: ₹25–50 LPA in India, $120k–$200k+ abroad.
  • Top Roles / CFO / Partner: ₹50 LPA+ in India, $200k+ internationally.


Disclaimer: Salaries vary widely based on company, industry, country, location, experience, and negotiation.
